solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dressed to kill

parts.note: the idiom for glamorous dress is read as looking so stunning that onlookers fall down lifeless

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for dressing to impress is taken literally: someone so stunning that they could kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dressed to kill is strikingly attractive, the idiom for extreme good looks.

clue.text: Epic climber approach with oddly drip-dry clothing

indicators.note: clothing means the selected letters wrap around the other pieces like a garment
oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of drip-dry

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant
to approach is to come

explanation.surface: A mountaineer setting out on an epic climb in drip-dry outdoor gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps the odd-placed letters of drip-dry, and 'clothing' wraps the first two and last two of them around the climber and the approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's long narrative poem of Hell, Purgatory and Paradise is a classic example of an epic.

clue.text: Cosmic model is at last okay after error corrected

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters before the final letter of okay
an error that is corrected gets put right, so its letters are set in a new order
at last picks the final letter of the word okay

explanation.surface: An astronomical model is finally passed as fine once a mistake is fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link here; the rearranged letters come first, since 'after' puts the last letter of okay behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system, showing planets orbiting the sun.

clue.text: Italian "dirge" he composed?

indicators.note: composed suggests musical writing but here means the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether an Italian wrote a mournful funeral song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges ITALIAN DIRGE HE into the poet's full name; the whole clue also describes him, an Italian who wrote of the dead in Hell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine poet who wrote the Inferno is fairly called an Italian author of lament.

clue.text: Hot stuff should not get left on top of staple food — that's greed

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top of puts the first piece above the second
should not get says the letter for left is to be removed from the hot stuff

parts.note: lava is molten rock, very hot stuff
rice is a staple food for much of the world

explanation.surface: A recipe warning that a hot topping mustn't be left on rice, followed by a moral comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot stuff' is molten rock from a volcano; 'should not get' strips the letter for left from it, and 'on top of' stacks what remains above the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is a synonym for greed, an excessive desire for wealth.

clue.text: Initially, Tony Blair's distortion of the family

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the name Tony
a distortion twists something out of its shape, so the surname's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jibe that Tony Blair twisted the idea of family values.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' gives T; 'distortion of' rearranges BLAIR as RIBAL. Tony Blair was a British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal means relating to a tribe, a group bound by family or kinship ties.

clue.text: Born again late Christian tea parties finally included

indicators.note: included means the final letters are taken inside the word for late

parts.note: something late in the sense of fresh or new is recent

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of each of the three words that follow it

explanation.surface: A born-again Christian, recently converted, invited to tea parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes N, A, S from Christian tea parties; 'included' puts them inside RECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means reborn or reviving, coming back into being.

clue.text: Take a second woman

parts.note: to take, as in a task taking a moment, is to be (it will be a moment)
a trice is an instant, a second

explanation.surface: An instruction to pause briefly, or to pick another woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a second' is read as 'be a trice': a job that takes a second will be a trice.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrice is a female first name, so a woman, as in Shakespeare's heroine.

clue.text: One missing from pack?

parts.note: suggests a missing playing card, but describes an animal living apart from its pack

explanation.walkthrough: 'pack' tempts you toward a deck of cards; it is a pack of wolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person who keeps apart from groups, like a wild canine living away from its pack.

clue.text: Porch is where flying raven had returned

indicators.note: flying means the bird's letters are scattered into a new order
returned means the word had is read backwards

explanation.surface: A raven flew back to the porch where it had been.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' turns RAVEN into VERAN; 'returned' turns HAD into DAH.
explanation.definitionFit: A verandah is a roofed porch or gallery along the outside of a house.

clue.text: Heard where blood flows to no useful purpose

indicators.note: heard says the answer sounds like the phrase that follows when spoken

parts.note: blood flows in a vein

explanation.surface: A lament that bloodshed was pointless, in medical guise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' signals that the phrase in vein, where blood flows, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something for nothing, without success, is an idiom for futility.

clue.text: See 14
Someone from Europe, and not the British, gain ground

parts.note: nor means and not
spoken by a Briton, the British are we

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters of gain are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A European, not a Brit, makes territorial gains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges GAIN as GIAN; the British speaking of themselves say WE.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Norway, a European country, is one example of someone from Europe.

clue.text: Material defects over

indicators.note: over means the word for defects is turned back to front

parts.note: warts, as in warts and all, are flaws or defects

explanation.surface: Fabric whose flaws have been overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns WARTS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw is dried stalks used as a material for hats, thatch and baskets.

clue.text: Manage to bring B and H together

definitions.meaning: to get by on limited money

definitions.text: to bring B and H together
definitions.meaning: B and H are the two extremes of the word ...

explanation.surface: Instructions to manage pairing two letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: B and H are both ends of the word both, so joining them makes both ends meet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have just enough income to cover expenses, to manage.

clue.text: See 3
Writer initially made way for extremely smart old printer

indicators.note: initially made way for says the first letter of the writer gives way to new letters

parts.note: a pencil is a writing instrument

indicators.note: extremely picks the two outer letters of the word smart

explanation.surface: An author first made room for a very stylish veteran printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially made way for' replaces P, the first letter of PENCIL, with ST, from 'extremely smart'. 'Writer' is a pen or pencil, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut template through which ink is pressed, an early form of duplicating device.

clue.text: See 1 across
River banks in Saigon troubled many soldiers

indicators.note: in places the river's outer letters inside the rearranged city
troubled means disturbed, so the city's letters are mixed up
banks are the edges of a river, so the outer letters of the word River

explanation.surface: A war scene of soldiers along a river in troubled Saigon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like a verb but means the edges of the word River; 'troubled' gives GAISON, and 'in' sets the edges inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a body of troops stationed in a town or fort.

clue.text: Pleasing oneself by refitting mansion

indicators.note: refitting a building rearranges its parts, so the letters of mansion are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone indulging themselves by renovating a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by refitting' rearranges MANSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Onanism is masturbation, a euphemism for self-gratification.

clue.text: See 14
See 14
Endearment supported by half of London wonder city

indicators.note: in a down entry, supported by puts the second piece underneath the first

parts.note: baby is a term of endearment for a loved one

indicators.note: half of takes the first three letters of the six-letter word London

explanation.surface: A sweetheart backed by half of London, a marvellous city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives LON from London, placed under BABY by 'supported by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon's Hanging Gardens were one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.

clue.text: See 1 down
Pains from smalls

parts.note: smalls are underwear in British slang, and tight underpants chafe and sting

explanation.walkthrough: Smalls is British slang for underwear; the stinging pains are the ones chafing underclothes cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarts are sharp stinging pains, the sort chafing underclothes inflict.

clue.text: Right about waistline

indicators.note: about means turned around or rearranged, so the letters of right are reordered

explanation.surface: A remark on measuring roughly round the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges RIGHT; it looks like 'approximately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is the measurement round the middle of a body, its circumference.

clue.text: Space for tied ribbon jumper found in tree

indicators.note: found in means the pieces sit inside the tree

parts.note: an elm is a tree
a bow is a ribbon tied in loops
a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

explanation.surface: A kangaroo with a bow on, stuck up a tree, needing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater, a common British word, but it is a kangaroo; 'found in' puts the ribbon and the animal inside the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is enough space to move freely.

clue.text: For starters: wine and cheese, coming up: fine fruitcake

indicators.note: for starters picks the first letter of each of the next three words
in a down entry, coming up means the word for fine is read upwards

parts.note: OK means fine

explanation.surface: A dinner menu: wine and cheese first, then fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For starters' gives WAC; 'coming up' turns OK into KO. 'fruitcake' is slang for a crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a crazy or eccentric person, in informal slang.

clue.text: Aphrodisiac may be part of a playboy's territory

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Seduction aids belong in a playboy's domain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are famously supposed to be an aphrodisiac, a food said to arouse desire.

clue.text: Permission for safe signal with nothing ambiguous

definitions.meaning: the siren after an air raid says danger is over

explanation.surface: Granting leave to signal safety, leaving no doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a go-ahead, a siren ending danger, or everything plainly understood.

clue.text: Small and dark? No

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
unlit means dark

explanation.surface: A question about a small dark place, answered in the negative.
explanation.walkthrough: S and UNLIT build the answer, and the closing 'No' tells you it means the opposite of dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathed in daylight is the opposite of dark, which the closing denial supplies.

clue.text: Mark manuscript as good and bad?

parts.note: Mark Antony, the Roman general

explanation.surface: Grading a manuscript with mixed marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a verb to grade, but is the first name of Mark Antony.
explanation.definitionFit: Good and bad are words of opposite meaning, an example of the plural answer, hence the question mark.
